{{Short description|Space-filling tetrahedron}}
In [[geometry]], the '''Hill tetrahedra''' are a family of [[Space-filling polyhedron|space-filling]] [[tetrahedron|tetrahedra]].  They were discovered in 1896 by [[Micaiah John Muller Hill|M. J. M. Hill]], a professor of [[mathematics]] at the [[University College London]],{{r|hill}} who showed that they are [[Hilbert's third problem|scissor-congruent]] to a [[cube]].{{r|sv}}

== Construction ==
For every <math>\alpha \in (0,2\pi/3)</math>, let <math>v_1,v_2,v_3 \in \mathbb R^3</math> 
be three unit vectors with angle <math>\alpha</math> between every two of them.
Define the Hill tetrahedron <math>Q(\alpha)</math> as follows:
<math display="block"> Q(\alpha) \, = \, \{c_1 v_1+c_2 v_2+c_3 v_3 \mid 0 \le c_1 \le c_2 \le c_3 \le 1\}.
</math>

A special case <math>Q=Q(\pi/2)</math> is the tetrahedron having all sides right triangles, two with sides <math>(1,1,\sqrt{2})</math> and two with sides <math>(1,\sqrt{2},\sqrt{3})</math>. [[Ludwig Schläfli]] studied <math>Q</math> as a special case of the [[Schläfli orthoscheme|orthoscheme]], and [[H. S. M. Coxeter]] called it the characteristic tetrahedron of the cubic spacefilling.{{r|coxeter}}

== Properties ==
* A cube can be tiled with six copies of <math>Q</math>.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://demonstrations.wolfram.com/SpaceFillingTetrahedra/|title = Space-Filling Tetrahedra - Wolfram Demonstrations Project}}</ref>  
* Every <math> Q(\alpha)</math> can be [[Dissection (geometry)|dissected]] into three polytopes which can be reassembled into a [[prism (geometry)|prism]].

== Generalizations == 
In 1951, [[Hugo Hadwiger]] found the following {{nowrap|1=<math>n</math>-}}dimensional generalization of Hill tetrahedra:
<math display="block"> Q(w) = \{c_1 v_1+\cdots +c_n v_n \mid  0 \le c_1 \le \cdots \le c_n \le 1\},
</math>
where vectors <math>v_1,\ldots,v_n</math> satisfy <math>(v_i,v_j) = w</math> for all <math>1\le i< j\le n</math>, and where <math>-1/(n-1)< w < 1</math>.  Hadwiger showed that all such [[simplex|simplices]] are scissor congruent to a [[hypercube]].{{r|hadwiger}}
